analysis:
This PR adds only two Swift test files under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Performance/: AdmissionRateEstimatorTests.swift and EngineMeasurementOrderingTests.swift. No production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, App Attest authorization, cache storage or fan-helper code changes in the supplied evidence. Unit 6106843e1203a899:0 is metadata only (added file, no lines to cite), and its content is covered by the :1 patch.

The tests exercise deadline admission rate estimation (DeadlineAdmissionFixes kill switch DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES, IsolatedPrefillAdmissionRate.resolve, decode-step shape, EnginePerformanceMeasurements ordering). They use a scripted PrefillScriptEngine, synthetic observations and a stub tokenizer. Nothing involves real prompts, keys, network or disk.

Threat relevance: the tests touch the T-010 and T-029 availability area (admission and deadlines) and the TB-007 inference engine boundary. They document a behavioral dependency the next pass should check against production code outside this batch. The fail-open stale-evidence expiry skips deadline projection on an idle engine after about 30 minutes (Policy.resolve returns nil). The kill switch defaults to on, and any explicit off value disables it. Those production semantics are not visible here, so I cannot confirm that they match the tests. The behavior concerns availability and latency admission, not confidentiality, and does not touch T-041 cache storage or the cacheSalt scoping.

The tests use no secrets and add no test hooks to production code. The only extension, `private extension EngineV2Bridge`, sits in the test target and relies on @testable access to pendingSubmissionIDs, so it cannot ship in the production binary.

No security regression or threat-model invalidation is identified from the supplied evidence. Remaining uncertainty is limited to the unseen production implementation, which this batch does not change.
